newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asian Metals - S.Korea traders fret over LG Metals.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - S.Korea traders fret over LG Metals.

text.p: South Korea metal traders were carefully watching any developments related to beleaguered LG Metals Corp, whose rumoured huge option-related copper losses continued to be a source of worry, dealers said on Thursday.
"We are nervous about the rumours, but there has been nothing to confirm them," one trader said.

On June 23, the country's finance ministry called in several local brokers to probe overseas futures trading by domestic firms after a sharp increase in South Korean metal derivatives trade through the London Metal Exchange (LME).

South Korea's base metal futures and options trade surged to 485,558 lots in the first four months of 1997 from 43,293 lots in the same period a year ago, according to data from the Korea Futures Association.
LG Metals spokesman Lee In-soo told Reuters on Tuesday the company had a "tight management system" for its futures operations and was closely monitoring its positions.
"The rumours that we are facing huge options-related losses on the LME are groundless," he said.
Last month Lee said the metals market had "no need to worry" about LG Metals open LME metal options positions, but he declined to comment on the rumours.
Meanwhile, traders said one European trader was seen actively buying Korean copper stocks to ship to Singapore.
"Sunjin Metals was said to have recently sold 3,000 tonnes of copper to Metallgesellschaft through the LME," one said.
Last week LG Metals said it had sold about 10,000 tonnes of copper supplied by Chile's Codelco to Metallgesellschaft and the cargo would be shipped to Singapore.
South Korea's sluggish domestic metal demand, stemming from a continued economic slowdown, has caused local traders to ship more stocks overseas to cut carrying costs.
The domestic aluminium market continues to worsen as more small- and medium-sized metal companies' defaults are expected, traders said.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery are still hovering between $95-$100 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash prices, they added.
Domestic aluminium prices were trading at between 1,520,000 won and 1,540,000 won a tonne this week, they said.

They said domestic aluminium sellers were seen trying to sell the metal at 1,540,000 won a tonne, while domestic were bidding 1,520,000 won following the results of the Office of Supply tenders for 2,245 tonnes of aluminium ingot.
Last week LG Metals won the government tenders at 1,520,000 won a tonne.
Domestic copper and zinc prices were flat at 2,467,000 won and 1,348,000 won a tonne respectively over the past week.
